thread_title: Suggestion For A Better Madness Mechanic

content:
—
to take some inspiration from limbus company & chaos zero nightmare, some ways to increase stage difficulties could be 

- disallowing / limiting DR procs

- disallowing / limiting turn rewind & restart battles 

- disallowing / limiting relics, for eg, u have to “ban” X amount of relics for more points, or use up to X amount of relic capacity 

- adding new mechanics mobs/elites/boss, for example, letting mobs get counter when they normally dont. or adding a berserk / enraged state if u do not follow a certain mechanic or do something wrong. 

- enemies get X amount of shield / healing every turn. 

- random encounter pop ups, in limbus mirror dungeon, there is a chance of getting “invaded” by a random boss. this could be very interesting if implemented in dtide. where a weaker boss could appear in an elite stage.

- stages that scale with your average team lvl, so say if your forbidden lore / average level of units is 90, all enemies and mobs will be that corresponding level. and u get a corresponding multiplier for how difficult it scaled.

content:
I’ve checked with other players. Without +12, the multiplier is 16%, and with +12 it becomes 48%, a 3x difference.

While I understand this is a bug, it has a major impact on the character’s performance. I hope the team will reconsider fixing Lotan’s pseudo-force multiplier.

This proposed change does not touch the character’s core gameplay and will have minimal impact on mainstream builds. Lotan does not rely on this mechanic for D-tide content either. However, the fix will outright invalidate several niche, alternative builds.

For example, stacking massive strike-growth via Midsummer. This 3x discrepancy will essentially kill that playstyle.

This specialized setup has very low general utility. It does not dominate the meta, cannot delete all content effortlessly, and only provides modest damage scaling. It is merely a niche, fun build.

Additionally, Lotan’s AA and Soulforge Aptitude  are all tied to strike based card plays, yet in practice, Lotan currently functions mostly as a fixed-damage support that rarely plays cards.

I believe this scaling growth effect could be retained as a feature. 

Mainstream Lotan builds have already shifted toward OE fixed damage.

All of Lotan’s 2.0 power gains are locked behind Soulforge upgrades. Even the buffs she received after the AA patch were Soulforge bound. Once Soulforge effects are disabled in the new chapter, she reverts to her original 1.0 state.

Compare this to the handling of 24 previously: the team retained that character’s base damage multiplicative scaling and even converted it into a final damage multiplier. That unit remains a top damage carry in New D-tide content to this day.

This scaling boost would have negligible impact given the massive HP inflation of high-difficulty enemies in the current environment.

Could the team consider keeping this mechanic and formalizing it as intended?

At minimum, please preserve this scaling bonus for Lotan as a signature playstyle, instead of reducing her to nothing more than a fixed-damage plug-in unit.

thread_title: Balance problem in arc2

content:
Two mechanics are really problematic IMO:  **Fervor** and **"When switching to this intent..."**.

By themselves, they are already hard to deal with but manageable, it does become a big problem when they are paired with many other situations the player also has to solve.

**Fervor** is even worse and limiting if you consider it's tied to arc 2 and Arithmetica Harmony. Playing more than 10 cards may not only make the enemy attack twice, but also makes your cards more expensive.

**Fervor** can also be really problematic when paired with enemies that have a passive against "non-command" cards. Feels like you can't play cards at all.

**Fervor** restricts team building too much IMO. You need such an absurd quality on your cards stats to overcome turn limit for achievements, while also surviving insane large hits. Currently done by using Saya+Vortice because you pair the best amplifier with an awakener based on Exalts and Posse instead of playing cards (with P-Caro and D-Aequor as a bonus).

Just to get things even worse, last chapter imposes a lot of limitations like Stagnation and Freeze. You need to use resources to deal with them, and those resources are often tied to playing cards (usually by getting Aliemus/Keyflare).

**"When switching to this intent..."** just has no counter aside from previous knowledge. It feels really cheap and wrong when the game is built around hoarding resources the whole investigation, to reach a boss, Exalt, and have your whole team Aliemus reduced because the Elite/Boss switched intentions. Even worse when/because it's random.

Difficulty and randomness are nice with moderation bu my experience with Morimens is each update getting closer to a glorified slot machine that I have to re-roll until a favorable result comes out. The game is getting a bit more interesting and complex, but also, way more annoying than it should be.
